name: Whitaker's Words (DICTLINE.GEN)
note: A Latin dictionary, for `lorem.word`. Lorem ipsum is Latin, and every permissively
licensed *digital edition* of a Latin text turned out to be CC BY-SA -- Perseus,
Wikisource, the Latin WordNet -- which does not compose with Apache-2.0. This is a
dictionary rather than a text, and William Whitaker's terms are unambiguous:
'Permission is hereby freely given for any and all use of program and data.'
Redistribution and commercial use are explicit; attribution is requested rather than
Only entries whose first stem is already a complete word are taken -- third-declension
nouns and adjectives, where the nominative is irregular and therefore stored whole, and
adverbs, which do not decline. Everything else in the file is a stem that needs its
declension ending to become a word, and reconstructing those means implementing Latin
morphology. Getting it subtly wrong would produce strings that look like Latin and are
not, in a language nobody reviewing this reads. 1,987 words survive that rule, against
Filtered to Whitaker's own frequency codes A through C, so the vocabulary is words a
Latinist would recognise rather than hapax legomena from the back of the corpus.
